en: Anna, how much is one kilo of tomatoes today?
tamil: அண்ணா, இன்னைக்கு ஒரு கிலோ தக்காளி என்ன விலை?
context: Asking a vegetable seller the price.
explain: 'How much' is used to ask the price of something. 'Today' shows prices can change daily.
usage: Use it at a vegetable market before you buy anything.
leelaQ: How much do you pay for tomatoes these days?
answer: I usually pay around thirty rupees for a kilo of tomatoes.

en: I will take two kilos if you reduce the rate.
tamil: நீங்க ரேட்டை குறைச்சா ரெண்டு கிலோ வாங்கிக்கிறேன்.
context: Offering to buy more for a lower price.
explain: 'If you reduce the rate' is the condition. 'I will take' is the result you promise.
usage: Use it while bargaining with a shopkeeper when you want to buy more.
leelaQ: What do you say when you want a better price in a market?
answer: I say that I will buy more if the shopkeeper reduces the price.

en: Please don't give me a plastic bag, I have my own cloth bag.
tamil: ப்ளாஸ்டிக் பை வேண்டாம், என்கிட்ட துணிப்பை இருக்கு.
context: Refusing a plastic bag at a shop.
explain: 'Don't give me' is a polite negative command. The reason follows after the comma.
usage: Use it at the billing counter when you carry your own bag.
leelaQ: Do you carry a cloth bag when you go shopping?
answer: Yes, I always keep a cloth bag in my scooter.

en: Is this mango sweet or sour?
tamil: இந்த மாம்பழம் இனிப்பா, புளிப்பா?
context: Checking the taste before buying fruit.
explain: 'Sweet or sour?' gives two choices, so the seller can answer in one word.
usage: Use it at a fruit stall before you buy mangoes.
leelaQ: Which fruit do you like the most?
answer: I like mangoes the most because they are very sweet.

en: Can you weigh it once again, please?
tamil: இன்னொரு தடவை எடை போட்டு காட்டுங்க, please.
context: Asking a seller to check the weight.
explain: 'Can you' with 'please' is a polite request. 'Once again' means one more time.
usage: Use it when you think the weight on the scale is not correct.
leelaQ: What will you do if the weight looks wrong?
answer: I will politely ask the seller to weigh it once again.

en: The vegetables here are always fresh in the morning.
tamil: இங்க காலையில காய்கறி எப்பவும் ஃப்ரெஷ்ஷா இருக்கும்.
context: Telling a friend why you shop early.
explain: 'Always' with the simple present talks about a habit or a regular fact.
usage: Use it when you recommend a market or shop to a friend.
leelaQ: When do you go to the market, morning or evening?
answer: I go in the morning because the vegetables are fresh.

en: I bought these bananas for forty rupees a dozen.
tamil: இந்த வாழைப்பழத்தை டஜன் நாற்பது ரூபாய்க்கு வாங்கினேன்.
context: Telling someone what you paid.
explain: 'Bought' is the past of 'buy'. 'A dozen' means twelve pieces.
usage: Use it when family or neighbours ask how much you paid.
leelaQ: What did you buy at the market last time?
answer: I bought some bananas and a few onions last time.

en: Give me a quarter kilo of green chillies.
tamil: கால் கிலோ பச்சை மிளகாய் கொடுங்க.
context: Ordering a small quantity at a stall.
explain: 'Quarter kilo' means 250 grams. Add 'please' to sound more polite.
usage: Use it at a vegetable shop when you need only a small amount.
leelaQ: How much chilli do you use for cooking at home?
answer: We use only a quarter kilo of chillies in a week.

en: You are charging me more because I am new here.
tamil: நான் புதுசுன்னு என்கிட்ட அதிகமா வாங்குறீங்க.
context: Complaining politely about a higher price.
explain: 'You are charging' describes what is happening now. 'Because' gives the reason.
usage: Use it when you feel a seller is asking a tourist price.
leelaQ: Have you ever paid more than the real price?
answer: Yes, once a shopkeeper charged me double at a temple market.

en: That shop is cheaper, so I am going there.
tamil: அந்த கடையில விலை குறைவு, அதனால அங்க போறேன்.
context: Walking away to a cheaper shop.
explain: 'So' joins the reason and the result. 'Am going' shows a plan happening now.
usage: Use it as a polite way to leave when the price is too high.
leelaQ: Do you compare prices before buying something?
answer: Yes, I check two or three shops before I buy.

en: Have you got change for a five hundred rupee note?
tamil: ஐநூறு ரூபாய் நோட்டுக்கு சில்லறை இருக்கா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper for change.
explain: 'Have you got' is a common way to ask if someone has something. 'Change' means small notes or coins.
usage: Use it at small shops when you only have a big note.
leelaQ: What do you do when a shop has no change?
answer: I pay by UPI or buy something small to get change.

en: We have been shopping in this market for ten years.
tamil: நாங்க இந்த மார்க்கெட்டுல பத்து வருஷமா வாங்குறோம்.
context: Telling a seller you are a regular customer.
explain: 'Have been shopping' with 'for ten years' shows an action that started in the past and continues.
usage: Use it to ask a regular seller for a better price.
leelaQ: Where does your family usually shop for groceries?
answer: We usually shop at the market near our house.

en: I never buy fruits from the roadside without checking them.
tamil: நான் ரோட்டோரத்துல பழம் பார்க்காம வாங்கவே மாட்டேன்.
context: Explaining your careful shopping habit.
explain: 'Never' makes the sentence negative. 'Without checking' means before checking.
usage: Use it when you talk about being careful with food and money.
leelaQ: How do you check fruits before buying?
answer: I press them gently and smell them before buying.

en: Keep the change, thank you.
tamil: மீதி சில்லறை வெச்சுக்கோங்க, நன்றி.
context: Telling a helper to keep the extra money.
explain: 'Keep the change' means you do not want the extra money back. It is polite with 'thank you'.
usage: Use it with an auto driver or a helper when you want to tip.
leelaQ: When do you give a small tip to someone?
answer: I give a small tip when someone helps me carry heavy bags.

en: The jasmine flowers smell so good today!
tamil: இன்னைக்கு மல்லிப்பூ ரொம்ப வாசனையா இருக்கு!
context: Enjoying the flowers at a flower stall.
explain: 'Smell good' describes the nice smell. 'So' makes the feeling stronger.
usage: Use it at a flower stall, or when someone brings flowers home.
leelaQ: Do you buy flowers for your house?
answer: Yes, I buy jasmine flowers every Friday for the pooja.

en: Could you show me the other colour as well?
tamil: மத்த கலரையும் காட்டுவீங்களா?
context: Asking a seller to show more options.
explain: 'Could you' is softer and more polite than 'Can you'. 'As well' means also.
usage: Use it in a cloth shop when you want to compare colours.
leelaQ: What colour do you like for your clothes?
answer: I like blue and green colours for my shirts.

en: He will bargain until the price comes down.
tamil: விலை குறையுற வரைக்கும் அவன் பேரம் பேசுவான்.
context: Describing a friend who bargains a lot.
explain: 'Until' shows the point where the action stops. 'Will' shows what he is going to do.
usage: Use it when you describe someone who likes to bargain.
leelaQ: Are you good at bargaining?
answer: Not really, but I try to ask for a small discount.

en: I can't pay more than three hundred.
tamil: முன்னூறுக்கு மேல என்னால கொடுக்க முடியாது.
context: Stating your maximum price.
explain: 'Can't pay more than' sets a limit. It is a firm but polite way to bargain.
usage: Use it when you want to end bargaining at your budget.
leelaQ: What do you say when something is above your budget?
answer: I say that it is too costly and I cannot pay that much.

en: Where can I find fresh coriander leaves?
tamil: புது கொத்தமல்லி தழை எங்க கிடைக்கும்?
context: Asking where to find an item in the market.
explain: 'Where can I find' is a useful way to ask for the location of a thing.
usage: Use it when the item you need is not at the stall in front of you.
leelaQ: What do you do when you cannot find something in a shop?
answer: I ask the shopkeeper where I can find it.

en: My mother always buys vegetables from the same seller.
tamil: எங்கம்மா எப்பவும் ஒரே கடைக்காரர்கிட்டதான் காய்கறி வாங்குவாங்க.
context: Talking about a family habit.
explain: 'Always' and 'buys' show a regular habit. 'The same' means not a different one.
usage: Use it when you talk about your family shopping habits.
leelaQ: Who does the shopping at your home?
answer: My mother does most of the shopping at home.

en: Please pack these separately.
tamil: இதெல்லாம் தனித்தனியா பேக் பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking a seller to pack things apart.
explain: 'Separately' means not together. 'Please' makes the order polite.
usage: Use it when you buy items that should not touch each other, like fish and fruit.
leelaQ: How do you pack things when you carry them home?
answer: I put the heavy things at the bottom of the bag.

en: I picked the best tomatoes myself.
tamil: நல்ல தக்காளியை நானே பார்த்து எடுத்தேன்.
context: Proudly telling your family about your choice.
explain: 'Picked' is the past of 'pick'. 'Myself' stresses that you did it, not someone else.
usage: Use it when you come home from the market and tell your family.
leelaQ: Do you like choosing vegetables yourself?
answer: Yes, I like choosing them myself so they are good.

en: Are these sarees handloom or machine made?
tamil: இந்த புடவைங்க கைத்தறியா, மெஷின்ல செஞ்சதா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper about the cloth.
explain: 'Handloom or machine made' gives two choices. 'Are these' is used for many things.
usage: Use it in a cloth shop when you care about quality and price.
leelaQ: What do you check before buying a saree or shirt?
answer: I check the cloth quality and the colour carefully.

en: I will come back after looking at two more shops.
tamil: இன்னும் ரெண்டு கடை பார்த்துட்டு திரும்ப வர்றேன்.
context: Politely leaving without buying.
explain: 'After looking at' is used with -ing. It is a polite way to leave a shop.
usage: Use it when you are not ready to buy now but may buy later.
leelaQ: What do you say when you do not want to buy something?
answer: I say thank you and tell them I will come back later.

en: Is this the final price or can we talk a little more?
tamil: இதுதான் கடைசி விலையா, இல்ல இன்னும் கொஞ்சம் பேசலாமா?
context: Checking if the seller can reduce more.
explain: 'Or' joins two choices. 'A little more' is a soft way to ask for more discount.
usage: Use it at the end of bargaining to see if there is room for a small discount.
leelaQ: How do you feel about bargaining at a market?
answer: I enjoy it because I can save a little money.

en: Where is the trial room, please?
tamil: ட்ரயல் ரூம் எங்க இருக்கு, please?
context: Asking a mall staff member for the changing room.
explain: 'Where is' asks for a place. 'Please' at the end keeps it polite.
usage: Use it in a clothes shop or mall when you want to try on clothes.
leelaQ: Do you always try clothes before buying?
answer: Yes, I always try them on so that the size is right.

en: Do you have this shirt in a medium size?
tamil: இந்த சட்டை மீடியம் சைஸ்ல இருக்கா?
context: Asking about the size of a shirt.
explain: 'Do you have' asks if a shop has something. 'In a medium size' names the size.
usage: Use it in a clothes shop when the size on display is not yours.
leelaQ: What size do you usually wear?
answer: I usually wear a medium size shirt.

en: This size is too tight around the shoulders.
tamil: இந்த சைஸ் தோள்பட்டையில ரொம்ப இறுக்கமா இருக்கு.
context: Telling the salesman the fit is wrong.
explain: 'Too tight' means tighter than is comfortable. 'Around the shoulders' says where.
usage: Use it in the trial room when you ask for a bigger size.
leelaQ: How should a shirt fit you?
answer: It should be comfortable and not too tight.

en: I would like to try a larger size.
tamil: நான் ஒரு பெரிய சைஸ் போட்டு பார்க்கணும்.
context: Asking to try the next size.
explain: 'I would like to' is a polite way to say what you want.
usage: Use it with a salesperson when the first size does not fit.
leelaQ: What do you do when a dress does not fit?
answer: I ask the salesman for a different size.

en: Please bring the same shirt in blue.
tamil: இதே சட்டையை நீல நிறத்துல கொண்டு வாங்க.
context: Asking the salesman for another colour.
explain: 'Bring' is a short command made polite with 'please'. 'The same' means identical.
usage: Use it in a cloth shop when you like the style but want another colour.
leelaQ: Which colour looks good on you?
answer: Blue looks good on me, so I buy blue often.

en: The mall is very crowded on Sundays.
tamil: ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை மால்ல ரொம்ப கூட்டமா இருக்கும்.
context: Talking about weekend crowds.
explain: 'On Sundays' shows something that happens every Sunday. 'Crowded' means full of people.
usage: Use it when you plan a shopping trip with friends or family.
leelaQ: When do you like to go to the mall?
answer: I like going on weekday evenings when it is not crowded.

en: We spent the whole afternoon at the mall.
tamil: நாங்க மதியம் முழுக்க மால்லயே செலவு பண்ணோம்.
context: Telling a friend about your day out.
explain: 'Spent' is the past of 'spend'. 'The whole afternoon' means all of the afternoon.
usage: Use it when you tell someone what you did over the weekend.
leelaQ: What did you do last weekend?
answer: We went to a mall and watched a movie.

en: This dress doesn't fit me properly.
tamil: இந்த டிரஸ் எனக்கு சரியா பொருந்தல.
context: Explaining why you want to return a dress.
explain: 'Doesn't fit' is the negative of 'fits'. 'Properly' means in the right way.
usage: Use it at the exchange counter or in the trial room.
leelaQ: What will you do if a new dress does not fit?
answer: I will go back to the shop and exchange it.

en: Is there any offer on this brand now?
tamil: இந்த பிராண்டுக்கு இப்ப ஏதாவது ஆஃபர் இருக்கா?
context: Asking about discounts in a store.
explain: 'Is there any' asks if something exists. 'Offer' means a discount or a deal.
usage: Use it before paying, to see if you can save some money.
leelaQ: Do you buy things only when there is an offer?
answer: Yes, I wait for an offer to buy costly things.

en: Buy one get one free is going on until Sunday.
tamil: ஒண்ணு வாங்குனா ஒண்ணு ஃப்ரீ ஆஃபர் ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை வரைக்கும் நடக்குது.
context: Telling a friend about a sale.
explain: 'Is going on' means something is happening now. 'Until Sunday' gives the end time.
usage: Use it when you tell someone about an offer in a shop.
leelaQ: What kind of sale do you like?
answer: I like sales where you get one more item for free.

en: Could you check if it is available in my size?
tamil: என் சைஸ்ல இருக்கான்னு பார்க்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking staff to check the stock.
explain: 'Could you check' is a polite request. 'If' here means 'whether'.
usage: Use it when the size you want is not on the shelf.
leelaQ: How do you ask for help in a big store?
answer: I go to the staff and ask politely for help.

en: I will pay in cash, so please give me a small discount.
tamil: நான் காசாவே கொடுக்கிறேன், அதனால கொஞ்சம் தள்ளுபடி கொடுங்க.
context: Offering cash to the shopkeeper in return for a discount.
explain: 'Will' shows a decision made now. 'So' joins the reason and the request.
usage: Use it at a small shop when you want to bargain a little.
leelaQ: Do you like to pay by cash or by card?
answer: I like to pay by card because it is quick and safe.

en: Can I get a bill with GST, please?
tamil: GST போட்டு பில் கிடைக்குமா, please?
context: Asking for a proper tax bill.
explain: 'Can I get' is a polite way to ask for something. GST is the tax added to a bill.
usage: Use it when you need an official bill for office or warranty.
leelaQ: Why do people ask for a proper bill?
answer: They need it for warranty or to return the product.

en: The billing counter is on the first floor.
tamil: பில்லிங் கவுண்டர் முதல் மாடியில இருக்கு.
context: Giving directions inside a store.
explain: 'Is on the first floor' tells the location of a place.
usage: Use it when you help someone find where to pay in a big shop.
leelaQ: How do you give directions inside a shop?
answer: I tell them which floor and which side it is on.

en: I have already tried this one on.
tamil: இதை நான் ஏற்கனவே போட்டு பார்த்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling the salesman you tried it already.
explain: 'Have already tried' shows the action is finished before now. 'Try on' means to wear clothes to check them.
usage: Use it when the salesman offers you the same item again.
leelaQ: Which clothes did you try on last time?
answer: I tried on a jacket and two shirts.

en: Don't remove the price tag, I may exchange it.
tamil: விலை டேக்கை எடுக்காதீங்க, நான் மாத்த வாய்ப்பிருக்கு.
context: Telling someone to keep the tag on a gift.
explain: 'Don't remove' is a negative command. 'I may' shows a possible plan.
usage: Use it when you buy a gift or something you may return.
leelaQ: What do you do if a gift does not fit?
answer: I exchange it for a different size.

en: Which floor has the men's section?
tamil: ஆண்கள் செக்ஷன் எந்த மாடியில இருக்கு?
context: Asking where a section is in a shop.
explain: 'Which floor' is used when there are many floors. 'Has' is used for what is on a floor.
usage: Use it in a big mall or department store when you are lost.
leelaQ: How do you find a shop inside a big mall?
answer: I read the board near the lift or ask the staff.

en: My sister is trying on a few kurtas now.
tamil: என் தங்கச்சி இப்ப சில குர்தாக்களை போட்டு பார்த்துட்டு இருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend where your sister is.
explain: 'Is trying on' shows an action happening now. 'A few' means some.
usage: Use it on the phone when someone asks where your family member is.
leelaQ: What are you doing right now?
answer: I am sitting at home and talking to you.

en: Hold these two shirts for me, I will be back in ten minutes.
tamil: இந்த ரெண்டு சட்டையையும் எனக்காக வெச்சிருங்க, பத்து நிமிஷத்துல வர்றேன்.
context: Asking staff to keep items for a short time.
explain: 'Hold these for me' asks someone to keep things aside. The second part tells how long.
usage: Use it when you need to go to the ATM or call someone before paying.
leelaQ: How long do you spend in a shop?
answer: I usually spend about half an hour.

en: That colour really suits you.
tamil: அந்த கலர் உனக்கு நல்லா பொருந்துது.
context: Complimenting a friend in a shop.
explain: 'Suits you' means it looks good on you. 'Really' makes the compliment stronger.
usage: Use it when you help a friend choose clothes.
leelaQ: What do you say to a friend who looks nice?
answer: I say that the colour really suits them.

en: I never buy clothes without trying them first.
tamil: நான் போட்டு பார்க்காம துணி வாங்கவே மாட்டேன்.
context: Explaining your shopping habit.
explain: 'Never' makes it negative. 'Without trying' is used with -ing after 'without'.
usage: Use it when someone asks why you spend so much time in a shop.
leelaQ: Why do you try clothes before buying?
answer: I try them to check the size and the comfort.

en: Will this shrink after the first wash?
tamil: முதல் தடவை துவைச்சதும் இது சுருங்குமா?
context: Asking about cloth quality.
explain: 'Will' is used to ask about the future. 'Shrink' means to become smaller.
usage: Use it when you buy cotton clothes and want to be sure of the size.
leelaQ: How do you wash your new clothes?
answer: I wash them in cold water the first time.

en: The sale ends tomorrow, so we should hurry.
tamil: சேல் நாளைக்கு முடியுது, அதனால நாம சீக்கிரம் போகணும்.
context: Urging a friend to go shopping soon.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. 'So' joins the reason with the action.
usage: Use it when you want your friends or family to shop before an offer ends.
leelaQ: Do you shop in a hurry or slowly?
answer: I like to shop slowly so that I do not make mistakes.

en: He bought a new pair of shoes yesterday.
tamil: அவன் நேத்து புது ஷூ வாங்கினான்.
context: Telling someone about a friend's purchase.
explain: 'A pair of' is used for things that come in twos, like shoes. 'Bought' is the past.
usage: Use it in casual talk about what someone recently bought.
leelaQ: What was the last thing you bought for yourself?
answer: I bought a new pair of sandals last week.

en: I forgot my wallet, so I paid through UPI.
tamil: பர்ஸ் மறந்துட்டேன், அதனால UPI-ல பணம் கட்டினேன்.
context: Explaining how you paid.
explain: 'Forgot' and 'paid' are past forms. 'So' shows the result of forgetting.
usage: Use it when a friend asks how you managed without cash.
leelaQ: What do you do if you forget your wallet?
answer: I pay with my phone using UPI.

en: My order was supposed to arrive yesterday.
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் நேத்தே வந்திருக்கணும்.
context: Complaining about a late delivery.
explain: 'Was supposed to' means something was planned but did not happen.
usage: Use it with customer care when your parcel is late.
leelaQ: Has an order of yours ever come late?
answer: Yes, my phone arrived three days late once.

en: Can you tell me where my parcel is now?
tamil: என் பார்சல் இப்ப எங்க இருக்குன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking customer care about a parcel.
explain: 'Can you tell me' is a polite way to ask for information. Then the word order is normal: 'where my parcel is'.
usage: Use it on a customer care call or chat about a delayed parcel.
leelaQ: How do you find out where your parcel is?
answer: I open the app and check the tracking page.

en: I ordered a phone cover online last night.
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி ஆன்லைன்ல போன் கவர் ஆர்டர் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Telling someone about an online purchase.
explain: 'Ordered' is the past of 'order'. 'Online' means on the internet.
usage: Use it in casual talk or when you start a complaint.
leelaQ: What do you buy online most often?
answer: I buy books and phone accessories online.

en: The delivery boy called me, but I could not hear him.
tamil: டெலிவரி பையன் போன் பண்ணினான், ஆனா எனக்கு கேட்கல.
context: Explaining a missed delivery call.
explain: 'Could not' is the negative past of 'can'. 'But' shows a problem.
usage: Use it when you explain why you missed a delivery.
leelaQ: What do you do when you miss a delivery call?
answer: I call back the delivery boy at once.

en: Please leave the parcel with the security guard.
tamil: பார்சலை செக்யூரிட்டிகிட்ட கொடுத்துட்டு போங்க.
context: Giving delivery instructions.
explain: 'Leave it with' means give it to someone to keep. 'Please' makes it polite.
usage: Use it when you are not at home and the delivery person calls.
leelaQ: Who receives parcels when you are out?
answer: My neighbour or the security guard receives them.

en: The app shows that my order is out for delivery.
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் டெலிவரிக்கு கிளம்பிடுச்சுன்னு ஆப்ல காட்டுது.
context: Telling family the order status.
explain: 'Out for delivery' means the parcel has left the warehouse. 'Shows that' introduces the news.
usage: Use it to tell your family to expect a parcel today.
leelaQ: How do you know when your parcel will come?
answer: The app sends me a message with the time.

en: How long will it take to deliver to Madurai?
tamil: மதுரைக்கு டெலிவரி பண்ண எவ்வளவு நாள் ஆகும்?
context: Asking a seller about delivery time.
explain: 'How long will it take' asks for the time needed. 'To deliver to' gives the place.
usage: Use it when you order from a seller in another city.
leelaQ: Do you like fast delivery or cheap delivery?
answer: I prefer cheap delivery if I am not in a hurry.

en: I have been waiting for the courier since morning.
tamil: நான் காலையிலேர்ந்து கூரியருக்காக காத்திருக்கேன்.
context: Complaining about a long wait.
explain: 'Have been waiting' with 'since morning' shows the wait is still going on.
usage: Use it when you call to find out why the courier has not come.
leelaQ: Have you ever waited a long time for something?
answer: Yes, I waited two hours for a courier last month.

en: Do you offer cash on delivery?
tamil: கேஷ் ஆன் டெலிவரி இருக்கா?
context: Asking a seller about payment options.
explain: 'Cash on delivery' means you pay when the parcel comes. 'Do you offer' asks if a service is given.
usage: Use it when you order from a small seller online.
leelaQ: Do you prefer to pay before or after delivery?
answer: I prefer to pay after delivery, so I feel safe.

en: I will track my order using this link.
tamil: இந்த லிங்கை வெச்சு என் ஆர்டரை டிராக் பண்ணுவேன்.
context: Telling the seller you will check the status.
explain: 'Using this link' tells the method. 'Track' means to follow the movement of a parcel.
usage: Use it after the seller sends a tracking link.
leelaQ: What information do you check while tracking?
answer: I check the date and the delivery city.

en: The product I received is different from the photo.
tamil: நான் வாங்கின பொருள் போட்டோவுல இருக்கிறதுல இருந்து வித்தியாசமா இருக்கு.
context: Complaining about a wrong product.
explain: 'Is different from' compares two things. 'I received' tells which product.
usage: Use it in a complaint to the seller or the app support.
leelaQ: What do you do when the product looks different?
answer: I take a photo and send it to the customer care.

en: Could you send me the tracking number again?
tamil: டிராக்கிங் நம்பரை திரும்ப அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
context: Asking a seller for the number.
explain: 'Could you' is polite. 'Again' means one more time.
usage: Use it in a message to a seller when you lose the number.
leelaQ: Where do you keep important order details?
answer: I keep them in my email and in my phone.

en: Free delivery is available for orders above five hundred rupees.
tamil: ஐநூறு ரூபாய்க்கு மேல ஆர்டர் பண்ணா டெலிவரி இலவசம்.
context: Explaining a shop's delivery rule.
explain: 'Available for' tells who can use the offer. 'Above' means more than.
usage: Use it when you tell a friend how to save on delivery charges.
leelaQ: How do you save money when you shop online?
answer: I add more items to my cart to get free delivery.

en: I always read the reviews before buying anything online.
tamil: ஆன்லைன்ல எதையும் வாங்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி நான் எப்பவும் ரிவ்யூ படிப்பேன்.
context: Talking about a safe shopping habit.
explain: 'Before buying' is used with -ing. 'Always' shows a regular habit.
usage: Use it when you give shopping advice to a friend.
leelaQ: Why are reviews useful?
answer: They tell us if the product is good or bad.

en: My package has not arrived yet.
tamil: என் பேக்கேஜ் இன்னும் வரல.
context: Telling support the parcel is missing.
explain: 'Has not arrived yet' shows something expected has not happened until now.
usage: Use it when you contact the seller about a late order.
leelaQ: What will you say to the seller about a late parcel?
answer: I will say that my package has not arrived yet.

en: Please call me before you come, I may be outside.
tamil: வர்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி போன் பண்ணுங்க, நான் வெளியே இருக்கலாம்.
context: Asking the delivery person to call first.
explain: 'Before you come' gives the time. 'May be' shows it is possible.
usage: Use it when you give instructions to a delivery person.
leelaQ: When do you ask a delivery person to call?
answer: I ask them to call when I am at work.

en: I am adding these two items to my cart.
tamil: இந்த ரெண்டு பொருளையும் என் கார்ட்டுல சேர்க்கிறேன்.
context: Describing what you do on a shopping app.
explain: 'Am adding' shows an action happening now. 'Cart' is the basket on a shopping website.
usage: Use it when you shop online with a friend and explain your steps.
leelaQ: What items are in your cart now?
answer: I have a pair of earphones and a book in my cart.

en: Is the delivery charge included in this price?
tamil: டெலிவரி சார்ஜ் இந்த விலையில சேர்த்தா?
context: Asking if the price has extra charges.
explain: 'Included in' means already part of the price. It avoids a surprise at the end.
usage: Use it when you order from a seller by phone or chat.
leelaQ: Do hidden charges bother you?
answer: Yes, I do not like surprise charges at the end.

en: The festival sale starts at midnight.
tamil: பண்டிகை சேல் நள்ளிரவு பன்னிரண்டு மணிக்கு ஆரம்பிக்குது.
context: Telling a friend about a sale time.
explain: The simple present is used for fixed events like a sale time. 'Midnight' is twelve at night.
usage: Use it around Diwali or Pongal when online sales begin.
leelaQ: Do you shop during festival sales?
answer: Yes, I buy clothes for the family during festival sales.

en: Don't forget to rate the seller after delivery.
tamil: டெலிவரிக்கு அப்புறம் விற்பனையாளருக்கு ரேட்டிங் கொடுக்க மறக்காதீங்க.
context: Reminding a family member.
explain: 'Don't forget to' is a common reminder. 'Rate' means to give stars.
usage: Use it when you remind a friend or relative after they shop online.
leelaQ: Do you give ratings after a delivery?
answer: Yes, I give a rating if the service is good.

en: They said I will get the refund in seven days.
tamil: ஏழு நாள்ல ரீஃபண்ட் கிடைக்கும்னு சொன்னாங்க.
context: Reporting what customer care said.
explain: 'They said' reports someone's words. 'Will get' talks about a promise for the future.
usage: Use it when you tell someone what support told you.
leelaQ: How long does a refund take usually?
answer: It usually takes about a week.

en: Which coupon code should I use for this order?
tamil: இந்த ஆர்டருக்கு எந்த கூப்பன் கோடு யூஸ் பண்ணணும்?
context: Asking a friend about a discount code.
explain: 'Which' is used when there are a few choices. 'Should' asks for advice.
usage: Use it when you shop online and need a friend's advice on discounts.
leelaQ: Do you use coupon codes when you shop?
answer: Yes, I search for a coupon code before I pay.

en: My cousin returned the shoes because they were too small.
tamil: என் cousin ஷூவை ரொம்ப சின்னதா இருந்ததால திருப்பி கொடுத்தான்.
context: Telling why someone returned a product.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Too small' means smaller than needed.
usage: Use it when you talk about online shopping problems.
leelaQ: Why do people return things they order online?
answer: They return things because the size or colour is wrong.

en: Could you deliver it after six in the evening?
tamil: சாயந்திரம் ஆறு மணிக்கு மேல டெலிவரி பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking the delivery person for a time.
explain: 'Could you' makes the request polite. 'After six' gives the time limit.
usage: Use it when you are at work during the day.
leelaQ: What time are you free to receive a parcel?
answer: I am free after six in the evening.

en: I saved a lot of money during the sale.
tamil: சேல்ல நிறைய பணம் மிச்சம் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Sharing a good shopping result.
explain: 'Saved' is the past of 'save'. 'A lot of' means much.
usage: Use it when you tell friends about a good deal.
leelaQ: How much did you save last time?
answer: I saved almost five hundred rupees on a bag.

en: I want to return this shirt because the stitching is loose.
tamil: இந்த சட்டையோட தையல் தளர்வா இருக்கு, அதனால திருப்பிக் கொடுக்கணும்.
context: Telling the shop staff why you are returning a shirt.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Loose' describes bad stitching.
usage: Use it at the customer service desk of a clothes shop.
leelaQ: Have you ever returned something to a shop?
answer: Yes, I once returned a bag because the zip was broken.

en: Can I get a refund, or only an exchange?
tamil: எனக்கு பணம் திரும்ப கிடைக்குமா, இல்ல மாத்திக்க மட்டும்தானா?
context: Asking about the return policy at a store.
explain: 'Or' offers two choices. A refund means getting your money back.
usage: Use it at the billing counter when you want to return an item.
leelaQ: Would you prefer a refund or an exchange?
answer: I would prefer a refund because I do not need another item.

en: I have kept the bill, so you can check the date.
tamil: நான் பில் வச்சிருக்கேன், நீங்க தேதியைப் பாத்துக்கலாம்.
context: Showing the bill while returning a product.
explain: 'Have kept' shows you still hold the bill now. 'So' gives the result.
usage: Use it when a shopkeeper asks for proof of purchase.
leelaQ: Do you keep your shopping bills at home?
answer: Yes, I keep the bills for big things like a phone or a fridge.

en: There is a mistake in this bill, you have charged me twice.
tamil: இந்த பில்ல தப்பு இருக்கு, ரெண்டு தடவை காசு போட்டிருக்கீங்க.
context: Pointing out a double charge at the billing counter.
explain: 'You have charged' tells about a mistake that has just happened.
usage: Use it politely at a billing counter when the total looks wrong.
leelaQ: What do you do when a bill has a mistake?
answer: I show it to the cashier and ask them to check it again.

en: Could you please give me a carry bag?
tamil: எனக்கு ஒரு கேரி பேக் கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking for a bag at a supermarket counter.
explain: 'Could you please' is a very polite way to ask for something.
usage: Use it at a supermarket counter after your items are billed.
leelaQ: What do you carry your groceries in?
answer: I carry them in a cloth bag that I bring from home.

en: Is this the last piece, or do you have more in the store?
tamil: இதுதான் கடைசி பீஸா, இல்ல உள்ள இன்னும் இருக்கா?
context: Asking if more stock is available.
explain: This question asks about stock. 'Or' gives two possible answers.
usage: Use it when you like an item but want a fresh or undamaged one.
leelaQ: Do you check the stock before you go to a shop?
answer: Yes, I sometimes call the shop first to check the stock.

en: The delivery person left my parcel at the wrong house.
tamil: டெலிவரி ஆள் என் பார்சல தப்பான வீட்டுல வச்சுட்டுப் போயிட்டாரு.
context: Complaining to customer care about a misdelivered parcel.
explain: 'Left' is the past form of 'leave'. 'Wrong house' says what went wrong.
usage: Use it when you call the customer care of an online shop.
leelaQ: What would you do if your parcel went to the wrong address?
answer: I would call the delivery person and then the customer care.

en: I am looking for a gift for my sister, can you suggest something?
tamil: நான் என் தங்கச்சிக்கு ஒரு பரிசு தேடுறேன், நீங்க ஏதாவது சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a salesperson for gift ideas.
explain: 'I am looking for' says what you want now. 'Can you suggest' asks for advice.
usage: Use it with a salesperson when you are not sure what to buy.
leelaQ: What gift would you buy for your sister?
answer: I would buy her a nice handbag or a set of bangles.

en: The price on the tag is different from the price on the screen.
tamil: டேக்ல இருக்கிற விலையும் ஸ்கிரீன்ல இருக்கிற விலையும் வேற வேற.
context: Pointing out a price mismatch at the billing counter.
explain: 'Different from' compares two things. It is a polite way to point out a problem.
usage: Use it at a billing counter when the scanned price is higher than the tag.
leelaQ: Do you check the price when the cashier scans an item?
answer: Yes, I always look at the screen to see the right price.

en: Please do not pack it yet, I want to check the expiry date.
tamil: இன்னும் பேக் பண்ணாதீங்க, எக்ஸ்பைரி தேதியைப் பாக்கணும்.
context: Asking a shop assistant to wait before packing.
explain: 'Please do not' is a polite way to stop someone. 'Yet' means not now.
usage: Use it at a grocery or medical shop before you pay.
leelaQ: Do you check the expiry date when you buy food?
answer: Yes, I always check it, especially for milk and biscuits.

en: How much will it cost if I take three of them?
tamil: மூணு வாங்கினா எவ்வளவு ஆகும்?
context: Asking for a bulk price from a seller.
explain: 'If' makes a condition. Use 'will' in the main part to ask about the result.
usage: Use it when you want a better price for buying more than one.
leelaQ: Do you buy things in bulk to save money?
answer: Yes, I buy rice and oil in bulk because it is cheaper.

en: The shop gave me a free gift with my purchase.
tamil: கடையில நான் வாங்குனதுக்கு ஒரு இலவச பரிசு கொடுத்தாங்க.
context: Telling a friend about a free gift at a shop.
explain: 'Gave' is the past of 'give'. 'With my purchase' means along with what I bought.
usage: Use it when you share a good shopping experience with friends.
leelaQ: What is the best free gift you ever got?
answer: I once got a steel water bottle with a pack of groceries.

en: I am waiting in the queue at the billing counter.
tamil: நான் பில்லிங் கவுண்டர்ல வரிசையில நிக்கிறேன்.
context: Telling someone on the phone where you are.
explain: 'I am waiting' shows an action happening now. 'Queue' means a line of people.
usage: Use it on a phone call when you are late because of a long line.
leelaQ: Do you hate waiting in long queues?
answer: Yes, I hate it, so I go shopping on weekday mornings.

en: Do you have a bigger size in the same design?
tamil: இதே டிசைன்ல பெரிய சைஸ் இருக்கா?
context: Asking for a larger size in a clothes shop.
explain: 'Bigger' compares two sizes. 'Same design' means the one you like.
usage: Use it in a clothes shop when the size you tried is too small.
leelaQ: What size do you usually wear?
answer: I usually wear medium, but sometimes I need a large.

en: My phone has stopped working, and it is still under warranty.
tamil: என் போன் வேலை செய்யல, இன்னும் வாரண்டி இருக்கு.
context: Telling a service centre about a faulty phone.
explain: 'Has stopped' shows a result now. 'Under warranty' means the company will repair it.
usage: Use it at a service centre when something you bought breaks early.
leelaQ: What do you do when your phone stops working?
answer: I take it to the service centre and show the warranty card.

en: Will you be able to deliver it before Diwali?
tamil: தீபாவளிக்கு முன்னாடி நீங்க டெலிவரி பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a seller about delivery before a festival.
explain: 'Will you be able to' asks politely if something is possible in the future.
usage: Use it when you order something for a festival and need it on time.
leelaQ: What do you buy before Diwali?
answer: I buy new clothes, sweets and some crackers for the children.

en: I tried to apply the coupon, but it was not working.
tamil: நான் கூப்பனைப் போட முயற்சி பண்ணேன், ஆனா அது வேலை செய்யல.
context: Complaining to online customer care about a coupon.
explain: 'But' joins two opposite ideas. 'Was not working' tells about a problem in the past.
usage: Use it in a chat with customer support on a shopping app.
leelaQ: Do you use coupons when you shop online?
answer: Yes, I always look for a coupon before I place an order.

en: This is a bit expensive, can you come down a little?
tamil: இது கொஞ்சம் அதிகமா இருக்கு, கொஞ்சம் குறைக்க முடியுமா?
context: Bargaining politely at a street shop.
explain: 'A bit' makes the complaint softer. 'Come down' means reduce the price.
usage: Use it at a street market when you want to bargain politely.
leelaQ: Are you good at bargaining?
answer: Not really, but I try to ask for a small discount.

en: We always compare prices online before we go to the shop.
tamil: நாங்க கடைக்குப் போறதுக்கு முன்னாடி எப்பவும் ஆன்லைன்ல விலைய ஒப்பிட்டுப் பாப்போம்.
context: Talking about shopping habits with a friend.
explain: 'Always' shows a habit. 'Before we go' links two actions in time.
usage: Use it when you chat with friends about smart shopping.
leelaQ: Do you compare prices before buying?
answer: Yes, I check two or three apps before I buy anything big.

en: The cashier gave me back the wrong change.
tamil: கேஷியர் எனக்கு தப்பான சில்லறை கொடுத்துட்டாரு.
context: Telling a friend about a billing mistake.
explain: 'Gave back' means returned. 'Wrong change' means the money returned was incorrect.
usage: Use it when you tell someone about a mistake at a shop counter.
leelaQ: Do you count your change after paying?
answer: Yes, I always count it before I leave the counter.

en: Is there a return policy if I do not like the product?
tamil: பொருள் பிடிக்கலன்னா திருப்பிக் கொடுக்கற பாலிசி இருக்கா?
context: Asking about returns before buying online.
explain: 'If' starts a condition. 'Return policy' means the rules for sending a product back.
usage: Use it before buying an expensive item from an online shop.
leelaQ: Do you read the return policy before buying?
answer: No, but I will start reading it for big purchases.

en: I got a message that my order has been shipped.
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் அனுப்பிட்டாங்கன்னு எனக்கு ஒரு மெசேஜ் வந்துச்சு.
context: Telling a family member about an order update.
explain: 'Has been shipped' is passive. It tells what happened to the order, not who did it.
usage: Use it at home when you share an update about a parcel.
leelaQ: What are you waiting for from an online order?
answer: I am waiting for a pair of shoes that I ordered last week.

en: Please wait, I will check the stock at the back.
tamil: கொஞ்சம் இருங்க, நான் பின்னாடி ஸ்டாக் பாத்துட்டு வரேன்.
context: A shop assistant asking a customer to wait.
explain: 'Please wait' is polite. 'I will check' promises an action in the near future.
usage: Shop staff say this when an item is not on the shelf.
leelaQ: What would you say if a customer asked for something you did not have?
answer: I would say sorry and offer a similar item.

en: We need to buy groceries for the whole month.
tamil: நாங்க முழு மாசத்துக்கும் மளிகை சாமான் வாங்கணும்.
context: Planning the monthly grocery shopping with family.
explain: 'Need to' shows something necessary. 'For the whole month' tells how long it lasts.
usage: Use it at home when you plan a big shopping trip.
leelaQ: How often do you buy groceries?
answer: I buy vegetables every week and other groceries every month.

en: Could you gift wrap this, please?
tamil: இதை கிஃப்ட் ராப் பண்ணி கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a shop to wrap a present.
explain: "Could you" is a polite request. "Gift wrap" means to cover a present with pretty paper.
usage: Use it at a gift or clothes shop before a birthday or function.
leelaQ: Who did you last buy a gift for?
answer: I last bought a gift for my friend on her birthday.
